title: Fitted pulse gaps show no clear time-direction change in 99 selected CHIME Catalog 2 bursts
abstract: We test whether gaps between fitted pulses grow during a fast radio burst. In CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231, 99 selected events from 53 source labels have at least three fitted pulses. Equal source weights give a last-to-first gap ratio of 1.044. The 95 percent source bootstrap interval is 0.816 to 1.327. A source-level time-reversal test gives p = 0.732. Resolution, pulse separation and zero-tail checks include a ratio of one. One band-edge cut gives a weak increase, but it does not pass a correction for the control tests. The result does not establish a slowing emission process, a fixed clock, or a new source. Missing pulses, shared fits and instrument selection limit the test. No independent telescope data confirm the statistic. Original code, aggregate evidence, exact input provenance and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Last-to-first fitted pulse-gap ratios under each selection. Bars give 95 percent source-bootstrap intervals. The dashed line marks equal gaps. Controls overlap.
